test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 05 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following places experiences extreme cold in winter and pleasant weather in summer?
solution:
The Correct Answer is **Leh.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Leh** has an extremely harsh environment and one of the highest and driest inhabited places on earth.
 
• **Leh** climate is referred to as a “cold desert” climate due to its combined features of arctic and desert climates.
 
• The entire area is nearly devoid of vegetation with the exception of valley floors and irrigated areas, due to the following factors:
 
• These include wide diurnal and seasonal fluctuations in **temperature, from -40°C in winter to +35°C in summer**, and extremely low precipitation, with an annual 10 cm to 30 cm primarily from snow.
 
• **Due to high altitude **and **low humidity, the radiation level is amongst the highest in the world.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amritsar - **

 
 
• The climate of the district is characterized by general dryness except in the brief south-west monsoon season, a hot summer and bracing winter.
 
• The year may be divided in four seasons. The cold season is from November to March. The period from April to June is the hot season.
 
 
 
• **Chennai - **
 
 
• Chennai has a dry-summer tropical wet and dry climate which is designated **As** under the Köppen climate classification.
 
• Chennai lies on the thermal equator and is also coastal, which prevents extreme variation in seasonal temperature.
 
• For most of the year, the weather is hot and humid.
 
 
 
• **New Delhi -**
 
 
• The climate of New Delhi is a dry-winter humid subtropical climate (Koppen **Cwa**) bordering on a hot semi-arid climate (Koppen** BSh**) with high variation between summer and winter in terms of both temperature and rainfall.
